answer: Give each agent one karst nectar well. Work seeps down through layers of limestone checks before any nectar drips out, so a fake cannot rush a reward. To open a well, an agent posts a refundable deposit, assumed here at $4,000 per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost about $4 million up front. Random peer inspectors sample the seep at the nadir of each cycle, and a well caught faking loses its deposit and is sealed shut. Clean work over time lets the nectar flow faster. Like water finding its way through karst, honest work drips through slowly while copies hit solid rock.
